Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> National Beyond Degrees: New platform turns every Ghanaian skill into opportunity Source : Albert Kuzor 30 October 2026 9:00am Audio By Carbonatix
For millions of young Ghanaians, the search for work has meant the same story: send the CV, wait, hear nothing, and wait again. Today, a new Ghanaian platform says the waiting can end. Sankofa Job, a national employment platform built by Ghanaian company G&T Prestige Ltd, launched today across all 16 regions of Ghana, with a simple message for every job seeker: don’t wait.
Your skill is already a job. Sankofa Job connects people who need work with people and businesses who need workers. It is free for every job seeker, open to every Ghanaian with or without a degree or a CV, and protected by Ghana Card verification through the National Identification Authority (NIA), so that the people and businesses on the platform are who they say they are.
About one in three young Ghanaians aged 15 to 24 who want work cannot find it, and nearly two million young people are not in school, work or training, according to the Ghana Statistical Service. At the same time, the Cyber Security Authority has warned the public about fake recruiters and cloned websites that take money from desperate job seekers.
“Talent is everywhere in Ghana, but access is not,” said Anthony Akwasi Gyamfi, PharmD, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of G&T Prestige Ltd. “For too long, finding work has depended on who you know, what you can pay and how lucky you are. Sankofa Job is here to change that. Not some Ghanaians. Every Ghanaian.”
Sankofa Job pays special attention to Ghanaians who have long been left out of online hiring: masons, seamstresses, mechanics, hairdressers, caterers, technicians and the self taught. Most Ghanaians learn their skills outside formal schooling, and many have years of excellent work but no certificate to show for it.
Through Sankofa Job Gigs, anyone can post their skill and be booked by the hour, the day or the week, while every completed gig and rating builds a record that employers can see. Households and businesses can also post a need, from a plumber or tutor to extra hands for an event, and find verified, skilled people nearby.
“Don’t wait for your dream job to find you,” Gyamfi said. “You already have a skill, and somebody already needs it. Post it, get found, and earn while you build toward the career you want. On Sankofa Job, your skill becomes your CV.”
The platform makes three promises. No fees: job seekers never pay to register, search or apply. No fraud: every person and business is verified with the Ghana Card, postings are reviewed, and users can report anything suspicious. No silence: a personal dashboard lets job seekers follow every application, from the day they apply to the day of an offer.
Sankofa Job also offers Interview Prep, Skill Assessments, Mentorship from professionals in Ghana and the diaspora, a Graduate Hub for young people after school and National Service, an Events section for job fairs and trainings, and the Sankofa Blog, where Ghanaians at home and abroad share real stories about work.
From a single trader to a national company or NGO, employers can post jobs and gigs in minutes and reach verified Ghanaian talent in every region. G&T Prestige Ltd is leading by example as the first hiring employer on its own platform, preparing to recruit up to 100 graduates and offering curated weekly gigs so young people can earn while they pursue their goals.
“To every business owner, from the trader with one shop to the largest company in Accra: the people you have been looking for are here,” Gyamfi said. “Honest, skilled and ready to work.”
The name Sankofa comes from the Akan principle meaning “go back and get it.” For Gyamfi, it is personal. Born in Ghana, he left as a young man carrying only a book bag and his documents, with no suitcase, no warm jacket and no money, and arrived in New York in the February snow. He built a career as a pharmacist and pharmacy manager in Manhattan, and today divides his time between New York and Ghana.
“I left Ghana with a book bag. I came back with a bridge,” he said. “Someone opened a door
for me. Sankofa Job is how we open that door for every Ghanaian the old system left behind.”
Sankofa Job begins at home, working with businesses, universities, technical and vocational institutions and partners across Ghana, and plans to grow to connect Ghanaians in the diaspora who want to hire, mentor and invest at home. The company says it will publish verified results as the platform grows.
Sankofa Job is available from today at www.sankofajob.com. Registration is free for job seekers. Users are reminded never to pay anyone to get a job. About G&T Prestige Ltd: G&T Prestige Ltd is a registered Ghanaian company (Reg. No. CS251601025) based in Abuakwa, Kumasi, with connections to the Ghanaian community in New York. Its brands are Sankofa Job, Adwuma Pa Podcast and Ankoaa. Its motto is Cross The Bridge.
